s01.translation: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee, blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

s02.translation: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

w001.function: The angel's word at Lk 1:28; the received English keeps the old greeting “hail”.

w003.function: Ablative with “plena” (w004): full with what — with grace; the received English says “full of grace”.

w004.function: Agrees with “María” (w002); construes with the ablative “grátia” (w003).

w005.function: Subject with an understood “est”: the Lord [is] with thee.

w006.function: A fused form: “te” + “cum” (with) — with personal pronouns the preposition “cum” FOLLOWS the pronoun: tecum, nobíscum.

w007.function: “Blessed [art] thou” — understood “es”. In the Vulgate these words still belong to the angel's greeting (Lk 1:28).

w012.function: Now of the fruit, not of Mary — masculine after “fructus” (w013).

w014.function: Fruit of what — of the womb; genitive with “fructus” (w013).

w017.function: Opens the petitionary half of the prayer; agrees with “María” (w018).

w025.function: The first of the two moments of the petition: now — and at the hour of death.

w028.function: Ablative after “in” (w027) — when; the received English says “at the hour”.

w029.function: At the hour of what — of death; genitive with “hora” (w028).
